table.title: MCP Auth Sessions
table.description: Per-user credentials stored for MCP servers (OAuth tokens and submitted headers), plus any pending authentication flows.

columns.typeTooltip: OAuth: per-user OAuth credential, either a stored token from a completed sign-in, or a pending sign-in flow. Headers: per-user header values (API keys / signed tokens), either stored or pending submission.
columns.boundToTooltip: The identity this credential is keyed to: an end user (via SSO), a virtual key (shared by anyone using that VK), or a client-issued session ID (asserted via the x-bf-mcp-session-id header).
columns.statusTooltip: Active: credential valid and usable. Pending: OAuth flow in progress, user must complete sign-in. Needs re-auth: upstream credential expired or revoked at the provider; user must reconnect. Needs update: the admin changed the required header keys; user must resubmit. Orphaned: the user lost access to this MCP (e.g. an access profile change); credential is preserved and will become Active automatically if access is restored.
columns.accessTokenExpiryTooltip: When the current access token expires. Bifrost auto-refreshes using the refresh token on the next request, so an active row past its expiry will silently mint a new token at use time. Header rows do not have an upstream expiry; their values stay valid until revoked or the schema changes.

table.empty: No sessions yet. Sessions appear here when an inference request or MCP gateway call triggers per-user authentication (OAuth or header submission).

revokeDialog.headerDescription: Bifrost will remove the stored credential values for this binding. There is no upstream token to revoke; the user will need to resubmit their header values to use this MCP again.
revokeDialog.sessionDescription: Bifrost will remove the stored credential for this binding. The upstream OAuth token is not revoked at the provider; it stays detached and expires naturally. Anyone using this binding will need to re-authenticate to obtain a fresh token.

missingFlow.title: Missing flow identifier
missingFlow.body: This URL is missing the <1>flow</1> query parameter. Open the link from your inference response or the sessions tab.

notYours.body: The pending flow belongs to a different identity. Ask the teammate whose VK or user identity triggered the original request to complete it, or trigger a new request yourself.

expired.oauthTitle: This authentication flow has expired or been completed
expired.oauthBody: Pending flows expire after a short window. If you still need to authenticate, trigger the original action again so a fresh flow is created.
expired.headersTitle: This submission link has expired or been used
expired.headersBody: Submission flows expire after a short window. Trigger the original request again to get a fresh link.

loadError.oauthTitle: Could not load this authentication flow
loadError.headersTitle: Could not load this submission link

invalidLink.title: This authentication link is no longer valid
invalidLink.body: The link may have expired, been used already, invalid, or had its short-lived token stripped. Trigger the original action again so a fresh authentication link is created.

auth.reauthBody: An active credential already exists for the binding below. Completing this flow will replace it with a fresh credential. You can also close this tab to keep using the existing one.
auth.freshBody: You'll be redirected to the provider to sign in and grant access. Bifrost stores the resulting credential against the binding below so this request and future ones can proceed automatically.

completed.noLongerCompletable: This authentication flow can no longer be completed
completed.credentialAlreadyStored: The OAuth credential for {{name}} is already stored. You can close this tab.
completed.triggerAgain: Trigger the original action again so a fresh flow is created.

headersAuth.savedBody: Bifrost verified the connection and stored your credentials. You can close this tab and retry the original action.
headersAuth.editBody: This server already has stored credentials for you. Submitting new values replaces the existing entry; the server will be re-verified before saving.
headersAuth.freshBody: This server requires you to supply your own API keys / tokens. The values you submit are stored encrypted and only used to authenticate your own requests.

authSuccess.title: Authentication successful
authSuccess.body: Your credential has been stored. You can close this tab and return to your MCP client - future requests will use this credential automatically.

authFailed.title: Authentication failed
authFailed.defaultError: We couldn't complete the authentication flow.
authFailed.body: You can close this tab and retry the original request from your MCP client to generate a fresh authentication link.
